question: How many candidates will officially remain in the UN Secretary-General race as of October 3, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 11-day windows in the endgame of a UN SG selection, measuring net change in the official nominee list; the modal window has zero changes, so the status-quo anchor is the current field. The field is 7, not the 8 stated in the criteria: Bachelet quit on 19-21 Sept after a 1-11-3 third straw poll, and Reuters, CFR, L'Humanite and Wikipedia all report seven remaining. Two forces move it off 7. Downward: A-Baki has taken 0 encourage votes twice, Sall (5-9-1), Otunnu (5-7-3) and Espinosa (3-6-6) are all weak, and high-level week is prime withdrawal-brokering time - but the usual trigger, a straw poll, is expected after 28 Sept under the October Greek presidency, i.e. likely past the deadline. Upward: 2016's direct analog window saw a late entry (Bulgaria nominating Georgieva on 28 Sept 2016), and 1for8billion lists rumoured entrants, so a last-minute nomination is live but unlikely. A separate instrument risk keeps real mass at 8: the un.org page still shows only Chile's 25 March co-nomination letter for Bachelet with no full-withdrawal notation, and the fine print counts only nominations 'recorded as withdrawn on that page' - though the credible-sources clause and 11 days for a Brazil/Mexico letter argue it resolves at 7. Net: ~0.69 on 7, ~0.14 on 8, ~0.13 on 6.
calls.dossier:
RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the official UN page 'Selection and Appointment of the Next Secretary-General' (un.org/en/sg-selection-and-appointment) — the count of nominees NOT recorded there as fully withdrawn — not off press reports, unless that page is unavailable or ambiguous, in which case credible sources reporting the official list govern. A profile may remain displayed while the nomination is recorded withdrawn; only the withdrawal notation counts.

EVENT WINDOW: 2026-09-18 (the criteria's stated 8-candidate snapshot) -> 2026-10-02 23:59 UTC; 14.0 days. As of Now 2026-09-22T14:10Z, ~29% elapsed.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: no change to the official list between now and 2026-10-02.

[PassBlue, 2026-09-18; Reuters/US News, 2026-09-18]

- 2026-09-21 and 2026-09-22: CFR and L'Humanite both describe seven candidates in the race. [CFR 2026-09-21; L'Humanite 2026-09-22]
- As of 2026-09-22T14:10Z the official UN page lists nine nominee entries; the only withdrawal notations shown are 'withdrawal of nomination of Virginia Gamba by the Maldives, 25 March 2026' and 'withdrawal of nomination of Michelle Bachelet Jeria by Chile, 25 March 2026' (the co-nomination letter; Brazil and Mexico nominations shown without withdrawal). No Bachelet full-withdrawal letter is posted yet. [un.org, fetched 2026-09-22]

- Formal removal requires a letter from the nominating state(s): Bachelet's live nomination rests with Brazil and Mexico. No report found of a Brazil/Mexico letter as of 2026-09-22.
- Fourth straw poll: no date set. PassBlue reports it could come after the General Assembly high-level week concludes on 2026-09-28, and that Greece takes the Council presidency in October and may set the timing. Color-coded (P5-distinguishing) ballots are expected later in the process. [PassBlue 2026-09-18]
- UNGA high-level week runs 2026-09-22 to 2026-09-28. [Al Jazeera 2026-09-22]
- Late entries have occurred in this race as recently as 2026-08-17 (Tonga nominating Ivonne A-Baki). 1for8billion maintains a 'rumoured potential candidates' list of 8 names (incl. Ardern, Mottley, Georgieva) explicitly labelled speculation, with no confirmed intent.
- No prediction market prices the number of remaining candidates (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi checked); Polymarket's only related contract is a winner market, a different resolution object.

BASE RATES
- Over ALL 11-day windows in this race since the process opened 2025-11-25 (~300 days): 11 changes to the official list (9 additions: Grossi 26 Nov 2025, Bachelet 2 Feb, Sall 2 Mar, Grynspan 3 Mar, Gamba 11 Mar, Espinosa 11 May, Rodrigues Birkett 15 Jun, Otunnu 24 Jul, A-Baki 17 Aug; 2 full withdrawals: Gamba 25 Mar, Bachelet Sep) -> ~0.4 list changes per 11-day window; most windows contain zero.
- CONDITIONAL on the endgame phase (after straw polls begin), the mix inverts: additions ~1 (A-Baki, 17 Aug, i.e. before polls 2-3), withdrawals ~1 (Bachelet). Changes cluster within 1-3 days AFTER a straw poll, not between polls.
- Over the 2016 race, withdrawals: Pusic 4 Aug, Luksic 23 Aug, Figueres 12 Sep — each following a poor straw poll (polls held 21 Jul, 5 Aug, 29 Aug, 9 Sep, 26 Sep, 5 Oct 2016). In the directly analogous 22 Sep - 2 Oct 2016 window, the list change was an ADDITION: Bulgaria nominated Kristalina Georgieva on 28 Sep 2016; no withdrawal is recorded in that specific window despite a 26 Sep straw poll.
- Conditional on a straw poll occurring in a window, 2016 suggests roughly 1 withdrawal follows within days in perhaps half of rounds; conditional on NO poll in the window, withdrawals in both races are rare.

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: any announced date for the fourth straw poll; any statement by A-Baki, Espinosa, Otunnu or Sall about withdrawing or staying in after 18 Sep; any Brazil/Mexico letter formalising Bachelet's exit; any confirmed new nomination in preparation; any market or bookmaker pricing the candidate count; any stated UN practice on how quickly withdrawal letters are posted to the selection page.

Reference class is 10-day windows in the final quarter of an SG race: net change is usually zero, with withdrawals tightly clustered in the 1-3 days after a straw poll and entries possible at any time (no nomination deadline exists). No fourth poll is scheduled; PassBlue reports one could follow after high-level week ends 28 Sept, so a poll-triggered withdrawal may fall on either side of the 2 Oct cutoff. Downside mass (6 or fewer) comes from A-Baki (0/10/5) or Espinosa (3/6/6) quitting, tempered by revealed preference: both sat through two bad polls already. Upside mass (8) comes from a dark-horse nomination during high-level week - exactly what Bulgaria did with Georgieva on 28 Sept 2016, and consistent with Amani Africa's reporting of a push for an African consensus candidate - plus residual risk that a resolver reads the criteria's explicit 'Bachelet counts as active' clause literally. Fine print: a profile still displayed but recorded as withdrawn does NOT count; new nominations appearing as active DO count. EVENT WINDOW: 2026-09-18 (the criteria's stated snapshot of 8) -> 2026-10-02 23:59 UTC; as of Now (2026-09-22T14:10Z) ~31% elapsed.
- The criteria's stated baseline of 8 active candidates (incl. Bachelet) is dated 18 Sept 2026. Michelle Bachelet announced withdrawal 19 Sept 2026, reported 19-21 Sept (MercoPress 21 Sept; US News 20 Sept; PassBlue 18-19 Sept). The UN page fetched 22 Sept 2026 shows her row marked withdrawn.

- Poll dates so far: 30 Jul, 21 Aug, 18 Sept 2026. PassBlue (18 Sept): no date set for a fourth poll; it 'could follow shortly after the General Assembly's high-level week ends on Sept. 28'. UNGA high-level week runs 22-28 Sept 2026.
- A-Baki drew zero encourage votes in both the 21 Aug and 18 Sept polls and has not withdrawn as of 22 Sept 2026. Espinosa (3 encourage) likewise remains nominated.
- There is no nomination deadline in the GA/SC process: a state can transmit a new nomination letter at any point up to the Security Council's formal recommendation (per UN process documents and CFR/Reuters explainers).
- PassBlue (18 Sept 2026) reports member states 'speculating about possible last-minute entrants'; no specific name or nominating state identified. Amani Africa commentary (Sept 2026) argues the 18 Sept result opens space for an African consensus candidate. 1for8billion's 'Candidates and speculation' page lists persons who have expressed interest without any formal nomination (Cahen-Salvador, Choquehuanca, Donat).
- BASE RATES, per class. (a) Over all 10-day windows from the first straw poll to the SC recommendation in 2016: 3 full withdrawals occurred across ~78 days (Pusic 4 Aug, Luksic 23 Aug, Figueres 12 Sept) ~= 0.4 withdrawals per 10-day window. (b) CONDITIONAL on the window being the late-Sept/pre-October stretch AFTER a poll has already happened and before the next: 2016's 12 Sept-5 Oct stretch contained zero withdrawals despite 10 candidates and several polling near-zero. (c) CONDITIONAL on a window containing a decisive/colour-coded poll: 2006 saw withdrawals within days (Tharoor 2 Oct 2006, after the 2 Oct poll). (d) New-nomination arrivals in 2026 over the last four months: 11 May, 15 Jun, 24 Jul, 17 Aug = ~0.4 per 10-day window. (e) Late entrants in the analogous 2016 window: Bulgaria nominated Georgieva on 28 Sept 2016 while Bokova's nomination stayed on the list.
- Withdrawal-to-page-update lag observed this cycle: Bachelet's 19 Sept announcement was reflected on the UN page within ~3 days.
- MARKETS: Polymarket lists 'Next Secretary-General of the United Nations' (winner identity, ~$122k traded as of mid-June 2026). No market found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi on the NUMBER of candidates remaining, and no bookmaker line found.

- STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: the official UN page on 2 Oct 2026 shows the same seven non-withdrawn nominees it shows on 22 Sept 2026.
calls.reference_class: 10-day windows in the final three months of past UN Secretary-General selections (2006, 2016, 2026 to date): net change in the number of officially active nominations

calls.reasoning: The stated baseline of 8 is already outdated: Bachelet fully withdrew on 19 Sep 2026 after a 1-encourage/11-discourage third straw poll, and the UN page, Wikipedia and wire coverage now describe seven active nominees. So the status-quo answer is 7, with ~8% residual risk the resolver still counts Bachelet (page-update lag or a literal reading of the criteria's Bachelet clause), which is the main upside contributor alongside a late entrant. Downside requires a further withdrawal in 11 days with no straw poll scheduled before 2 Oct - the post-poll-3 attrition has already been absorbed, and A-Baki (0 encourage), Espinosa and Sall have all been reported as still in as of 21 Sep. In 2016 weak candidates mostly stayed on the ballot to the final colour-coded poll rather than exiting mid-window, which argues against multiple exits. Upside: 2016 (Georgieva, 28 Sep) and 2006 (Zeid, Vike-Freiberga) both saw fresh nominations in exactly this late-September slot, and diplomats are openly canvassing last-minute entrants since no candidate has cleared P5 veto risk; I price ~15% on at least one new nomination appearing as active on the UN page by 2 Oct. Net: mass concentrated on 7, meaningful secondary mass on 6 and 8.

calls.reasoning: The criteria's 8-candidate baseline is one stale: Bachelet withdrew 19 Sep after collapsing to 1-11-3 in the 18 Sep straw poll, and press, CFR and Wikipedia all now count seven. The modal 11-day endgame window has zero net change, and the usual withdrawal trigger — the next straw poll — is expected only after high-level week ends 28 Sep, likely past the 2 Oct cutoff. Downside (6 or less) needs a weak candidate (A-Baki 0 encourage twice, Espinosa 3-6-6, Sall 5-9-1) to quit during high-level week despite revealed preference to stay. Upside (8) comes from a late nomination letter circulating — the exact thing Bulgaria did with Georgieva on 28 Sep 2016, with Nusseibeh/Kaag/African-consensus names openly canvassed now — plus residual instrument risk that the UN page still shows only Chile's 25 March co-nomination letter and a resolver reads the Bachelet clause literally; the page-ambiguity fallback to credible sources argues that lands at 7 anyway.
calls.reconciliation: Three disputes were factual. (1) Whether the UN page already records Bachelet's full withdrawal: Run 2 said yes, Run 1 said no, and Run 3's fetch — flagged withdrawn but dated 25 Mar 2026 — corroborates Run 1, since 25 March is Chile's co-nomination letter, the exact item the criteria say does NOT deactivate her. I settle this as 'full-withdrawal letter probably not yet posted', which raises instrument risk but does not flip the answer, because the fine print routes an ambiguous page to credible sources and all of them say seven; ~7% residual on 8. (2) Whether Bachelet actually withdrew: settled yes, unanimous across dossiers and four outlets. (3) Whether a fourth straw poll falls before the cutoff: settled no date set; expected after 28 Sep. The remaining two disputes are pure judgment with no evidence to break them — late-entrant probability (~12%, precedent-backed but requires a letter to circulate, and GRULAC rotation cuts against non-regional entrants) and further-withdrawal probability (~20% for one, ~4% for two, with post-poll-3 attrition already absorbed). No web access this run, so nothing was re-verified against un.org directly; the Bachelet page-notation finding rests on cross-reading the three dossiers' own fetches. No market prices field size on any venue the runs checked, so nothing was blended.
